Package de.hof.dms.service

Class FolderService

java.lang.Object
de.hof.dms.service.FolderService
@Service @Profile("!no-mongo") public class FolderService extends Object
Manages the folder tree: viewing, listing, creating, renaming/moving, and deleting folders. Folders use a materialized path so a whole subtree can be rewritten or removed in one pass. Every operation enforces access through PermissionService, and listings only ever return folders and documents the caller may read.

    • listFolders

      public FolderPage listFolders(String parentId, int page, int size, CurrentUser user)
      Lists the child folders of parentId (or of the root folder when parentId is blank), restricted to folders the caller may read, with pagination applied after the permission filter so the totals reflect what the caller can actually see. Requires read on the parent folder.

    • createFolder

      public FolderResponse createFolder(CreateFolderRequest request, CurrentUser user)
      Creates a folder under the given parent (or under the root folder when no parent is supplied). The materialized path is derived from the parent path, the ACL is seeded from the creating user's identity, and a second root folder can never be created because a non-empty name always produces a path other than "/".

    • updateFolder

      public FolderResponse updateFolder(String id, UpdateFolderRequest request, CurrentUser user)
      Renames and/or moves a folder. The materialized path of the folder and of its entire subtree is rewritten so paths stay consistent. Requires update on the folder, plus create on the destination parent when moving. The root folder cannot be modified, a folder cannot be moved into itself or a descendant, and the destination must not already contain a sibling with the same name.

    • deleteFolder

      public void deleteFolder(String id, boolean recursive, CurrentUser user)
      Deletes a folder. Requires delete on the folder; the root folder can never be deleted. A non-empty folder is rejected unless recursive is set, in which case the whole subtree is removed and the documents it contains are soft-deleted.
